clue.text: Find junk — drug's wanted for fixes

parts.note: to junk something is to scrap it
E is ecstasy, so E's is its plural or possessive

explanation.surface: Someone rummaging through rubbish while craving a drug fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixes' reads as drug doses, matching 'drug', but here it means awkward predicaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapes and fixes are both informal words for awkward situations or predicaments one gets into.

clue.text: With spiky hair style and stockings, but topless!

indicators.note: topless means the head of the word, its first letter, is missing

parts.note: a hair set is a style
hose is an old word for stockings

explanation.surface: A punk with spiky hair wearing stockings and nothing on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Setose is a biological term meaning bristly, covered with stiff hairs or bristles.

clue.text: Is that so English, breaking in to banter?

indicators.note: breaking in means forcing a way inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a rally is a lively exchange of words, as in old usage
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A query whether an English person has really joined in a bout of teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Really, said as a question, expresses surprise exactly as 'is that so?' does.

clue.text: Couple with baby may be Sebastian and Viola

definitions.text: Couple with baby may be Sebastian and Viola

parts.note: surface reading: parents with an infant, choosing names for it
setter's reading: the boy and girl twins of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: New parents considering names for their child.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian and Viola are the brother and sister twins in Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon pair is a boy and girl twin pair, or a family's only two children of opposite sexes.

clue.text: Composition of this faculty is from all quarters

wordplay.note: the compass points South, East, North, South, East

explanation.surface: A university faculty drawing its members from all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' here are compass points; the faculty is a mental power, not a department.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense such as sight or hearing is a natural faculty or power of perception.

clue.text: Vehicle's uphill gear (hardly likely!)

parts.note: an uphill task is a hard one
gear is clothing, and a top is a garment

explanation.surface: A motorist doubts the car will climb a hill in its highest gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' suggests a car's gearbox, but it is clothing; the bracketed aside is the setter's joke about top gear on a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a motor car with a rigid, fixed roof rather than a folding soft one.

clue.text: Male flattery almost could be sincere

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else when rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's compliments might, for once, be genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt and sincere both describe feelings that are deeply and genuinely held.

clue.text: Run in the blood

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to run in competition, to sprint

definitions.note: a phrase for what the noun names
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ancestry, lineage inherited from one's forebears

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an idiom about inherited traits running in the blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a sprint contest, and also a people sharing common descent or ancestry.

clue.text: Moving about

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as moving around, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Touching means emotionally affecting, and as a preposition it means concerning or regarding a topic.

clue.text: Walks out, what satisfies the environment …

parts.words: Walks out, what satisfies the environment
parts.note: surface reading: going for walks is the green way of travelling
setter's reading: the routes one walks along outdoors

explanation.surface: Walking instead of driving is the eco-friendly choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathways are tracks or footpaths, routes along which people take walks.

clue.text: Finally, instrument with fret about to produce this sound

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that comes straight after it

parts.note: last letter of instrument

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for fret is read backwards

parts.note: to fret is to worry or gnaw away at

explanation.surface: A guitarist's finger on the fret makes the strings resonate.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is the resonant plucked sound of a string, exactly the noise a fretted instrument produces.

clue.text: Not a description of ne'er-do-well

definitions.meaning: first meaning: if there is ..., nothing has been described
second meaning: a worthless, idle good-for-nothing

explanation.surface: Someone declining to describe a good-for-nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-account is an American term for a worthless, shiftless person, the same as a wastrel.

clue.text: The outline's wrong — cutting out new one

definitions.note: refers back to outline: the answer is one

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of their proper order and need rearranging
cutting something out removes it from the letters it sits among

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A draughtsman complains that a sketched outline has come out wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N from THE OUTLINES and rearrange to get SILHOUETTE; 'one' then points back to 'outline'.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is a dark shape showing only an object's profile, so it is itself an example of an outline.

clue.text: Dog food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue
second meaning: slang for grub or a meal

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as pet food, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The chow is a Chinese dog breed, and chow is also informal slang for meals or grub.

clue.text: Suspects hanky-panky in a smart sell, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the phrase is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wary buyer senses trickery behind a slick sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom for suspecting that something underhand or dishonest is going on.

clue.text: Weekly child allowance

parts.note: surface reading: a state benefit paid to parents each week
setter's reading: the small sum a parent hands a youngster to spend

explanation.surface: A government benefit paid to families every week.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocket money is the small regular sum parents give children to spend as they wish.

clue.text: Gallant companion to girl right out of fairy tale

parts.note: surface reading: a chivalrous escort for a young lady
setter's reading: a knight in shining armour, the rescuer of storybook maidens

explanation.surface: A girl's dashing escort who seems to come straight out of a storybook.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalier is a knight or cavalier, and by extension a chivalrous, courteous man.

clue.text: Girl is sallowy-grey

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a pale greyish-yellow colour

explanation.surface: A sickly-looking young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a feminine name and also a dingy greyish-yellow shade, named after a Spanish princess.

clue.text: Current resolution carrying sections of the floor

indicators.note: the phrase carries pieces of its words that make up a new word

parts.note: found inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: A floor plan being displayed at the current screen resolution.
explanation.definitionFit: An entresol is a mezzanine, a low floor between the ground floor and the one above.

clue.text: Romantic drove one out to lunch

parts.note: as in drove or sent someone mad
Roman numeral one
both are slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A romantic who drove a sweetheart out for a lunch date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out to lunch' looks like a mealtime outing, but it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentimental and romantic both describe someone moved by tender, nostalgic or loving feelings.

clue.text: Girl, sweetie, losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means its centre letter goes missing

parts.note: a caramel is a toffee sweet

explanation.surface: A lovelorn girl is called sweetie by her suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmel is a feminine first name, taken from Mount Carmel in Israel.

clue.text: Tight undercover operation by Yard

parts.note: a police sting is a covert trap
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A cash-strapped Scotland Yard undercover operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight and stingy both mean mean with money, reluctant to spend.

clue.text: Runs restricted by extra cover for Sussex, perhaps

indicators.note: being restricted by something means being hemmed in on both sides by it

parts.note: a bye is a cricket extra, a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket report: runs were kept down by the fielder at extra cover for Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is an English county with a cricket team, and also a breed of cattle; extra cover is a fielding position.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a cowshed, so it shelters cattle such as the Sussex breed.

clue.text: Invalid off

parts.note: something invalid is false or unsound
the off is the start of a race

explanation.surface: A sick person is setting off somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' reads as a sick person, but here means not valid; the two words build the answer and together also define it.
explanation.definitionFit: A false start is a race beginning that does not count because a competitor moved too early.

clue.text: Long time, no see? No, no!

definitions.text: Long time, no see? No, no!

parts.note: surface reading: a friendly greeting to someone not met for ages
setter's reading: strike out the no, leaving see, the act of seeing

explanation.surface: A greeting to an old friend, followed by an emphatic correction.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing 'no' leaves 'see', and the answer is both vision and 'a long time' in the slang sense of a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is the faculty of seeing, and colloquially 'a sight' means a great amount, such as a long time.

clue.text: Toddler''s up and showing bounce

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tot is a small child, here with 's

explanation.surface: A small child who is awake and full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Stot is a Scottish and northern English word for bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: To stot means to rebound or spring off the ground, as a ball or a leaping deer does.

clue.text: It's very late — stay another night

parts.note: to stay or endure is to last

indicators.note: another version of a word is a different arrangement of the same letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tired guest asks whether to stay one more night as it is getting late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another night' reads as an extra stay but asks for another arrangement of the word night.
explanation.definitionFit: Last thing means at the very end of the day, just before going to bed.

clue.text: Citizen for Queen and Country

parts.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen
a country in the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A patriot serving Queen and Country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman was a citizen of ancient Rome, the capital of an empire whose citizenship was prized.

clue.text: Answer to orbital complication, without one's heat shield

indicators.note: a complication tangles things up, so the letters are scrambled
without means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the fodder

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A space engineer seeks a solution to a problem in orbit involving the heat shield.
explanation.definitionFit: An ablator is a material on a spacecraft's heat shield that burns away to carry heat off during re-entry.

clue.text: Finger collaborator? Absolutely!

parts.note: a finger of whisky is a small measure, as is a tot
an ally works with you

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they will point out a traitor eagerly agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finger' looks like a verb for informing on someone; it is a measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally and absolutely are both adverbs meaning completely, used as emphatic agreement.
